Q: Should i learn two languages or stay with one? A:

I have a difficult time choosing between two things.

Why do you think you need to? They’re not mutually exclusive in any way. Learning one thing does not prevent you from learning another thing.

I certainly wouldn’t recommend constraining yourself to only learning one programming language. That’s just arbitrarily placing limits on yourself.

Even if other languages aren’t something you necessarily use in a professional capacity or even particularly often, by virtue of learning different things you’ll broaden your overall knowledge and understanding of programming in general.

Q: How to change the line length for Code wrapping in VSCode A:

It took me long to find but finally here in Stackoverflow. changing only editor.wordwrap in settings.json won't do it for Dart code/formatter, these setting I think is for general Vscode but should be added also:

{
   "editor.wordWrap": "wordWrapColumn",
   "editor.wordWrapColumn": 120,
   "editor.rulers": [120]
}

As for it to work for "Dart" code, these settings should be added:

"dart.lineLength": 120,
"[dart]": {
    "editor.rulers": [
        120
    ],
}

Thanks for all who answered in that question: Changing wordwrapping and formatting for Dart code in VSCode

FYI there are four modes for "editor.wordWrap":

Value Behavior
off Lines never wrap; you must scroll horizontally.
on Lines wrap at the viewport width (the edge of the editor window).
wordWrapColumn Lines wrap at the specific column number defined in editor.wordWrapColumn.
bounded Lines wrap at the minimum of the viewport width and the word wrap column.

There are also language-specific overrides, eg -

"[markdown]": {
    "editor.wordWrap": "on"
  },

Q: Selenium WebDriver receiving updates faster than Chrome A:

A few things going on here, and one important detail in your stacktrace: you're using undetected_chromedriver, not standard Selenium. That's likely why your ChromeDriverManager fix didn't work. undetected_chromedriver downloads and manages its own ChromeDriver binary, completely ignoring what webdriver-manager installs. The two are separate driver management systems, and uc.Chrome() was disregarding your service object entirely.

The quickest fix is to pin the ChromeDriver version directly in undetected_chromedriver:

import undetected_chromedriver as uc

driver = uc.Chrome(version_main=145)

This tells it to fetch the ChromeDriver matching your installed Chrome 145 instead of grabbing the latest (146).

If you'd rather update Chrome itself, go to chrome://settings/help. If it still shows "up to date" on 145, the auto-updater hasn't caught up yet. You can bypass it by downloading the latest installer from google.com/chrome, which typically ships the newest stable version. Alternatively, Google provides exact version downloads through Chrome for Testing at https://googlechromelabs.github.io/chrome-for-testing/.

Chrome for Testing is actually the most robust long-term solution. You download a specific Chrome binary and its matching ChromeDriver together, completely decoupled from your system Chrome:

import undetected_chromedriver as uc

options = uc.ChromeOptions()
options.binary_location = r"C:\path\to\chrome-for-testing\chrome.exe"

driver = uc.Chrome(options=options, version_main=146)

You can automate the download using the JSON endpoint at https://googlechromelabs.github.io/chrome-for-testing/last-known-good-versions-with-downloads.json.

Finally, if you don't actually need undetected_chromedriver, Selenium 4.6+ has a built-in Selenium Manager that auto-downloads a matching ChromeDriver with no extra libraries needed:

from selenium import webdriver

driver = webdriver.Chrome()

But for your situation right now, uc.Chrome(version_main=145) is the one-line fix.
